title: Canonical derived evaluation morphism and its triangle naturality
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the derived internal Hom on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and derived tensor computed after K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Put $F_{L,M}(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ and $G_{L,M}(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$. There is a canonical morphism $e_{K,L,M}:F_{L,M}(K)\to G_{L,M}(K)$, the transpose of the composite
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L\longrightarrow M,$$
where the first arrow uses the graded symmetry to evaluate the first and third factors into $L$, and the second is evaluation. It is natural covariantly in $K,M$ and contravariantly in $L$. For fixed $L,M$, both $F_{L,M}$ and $G_{L,M}$ are exact functors of triangulated categories, with the standard signed shift comparisons; $e$ commutes with those comparisons and sends each distinguished triangle in $K$ to a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the square on the connecting map. No invertibility of $e$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0A67 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more, signed chain-level construction), and 064J (lemma-derived-tor-exact); RHom exactness in literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated). The compatibility on connecting maps is the signed cone compatibility of this construction.

proof.text: Write $H(X,Y)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$. Apply the closed symmetric monoidal structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] on the one-object site with the trivial topology and constant ring $R$. Its modules are precisely $R$-modules; this site is small. Put $A=H(L,M)$ and $B=H(K,L)$. Form $A\otimes^L K\otimes^L B\to A\otimes^L B\otimes^L K\to A\otimes^L L\to M$, swapping $K,B$ and then applying the two counits. Transpose it under $-\otimes^L B\dashv H(B,-)$ to obtain $e:A\otimes^L K\to H(B,M)$. By naturality and involutivity of the symmetry, uncurrying instead with $B$ on the left gives exactly the composite in the statement: move $B$ past $A$, then evaluate $B\otimes^L K$, then evaluate $A\otimes^L L$. Thus this is a specified canonical map, without choices of an inverse or of a finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0A67, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate; Tag 0A60, lemma-evaluate-and-more and remark-sign-explanation

proof.text: The closed adjunction in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] is natural in all its variables. For $u:K\to K'$, the two uncurried composites reduce to evaluating $f\circ u$ on $x$, or $f$ on $u(x)$; the equality is the first-variable counit naturality. For $v:M\to M'$, they reduce to $v\circ h$ evaluated on $f(x)$, or $v$ applied after evaluation by $h$, which is second-variable counit naturality. For $t:L'\to L$, both reduce to $h(t(f(x)))$: on the source $h$ is precomposed with $t$, and on the target precomposition with $H(K,t)$ reverses the direction again. These are equalities of evaluation composites supplied by naturality of the adjunction, rather than an appeal to elements of arbitrary derived objects. Transposition, a bijection, gives the required covariant $K,M$ squares and contravariant $L$ square.

source.place: Tag 0A67, omitted functoriality argument, expanded using counit naturality

proof.text:
Choose K-injective representatives $J,I$ of $L,M$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $A^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(J,I)$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] (one K-flat factor and one arbitrary complex), and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $A^\bullet\otimes P$ represents $F(K)$ (use symmetry to put the K-flat representative first), and $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J),I)$ represents $G(K)$. The chain tensor--Hom bijection [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] identifies the transpose in step 1 with
$$E_P(h\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{bc}h(f(x)),\quad |h|=a,\ |x|=b,\ |f|=c.$$
The sign comes from swapping $x,f$; the evaluation maps themselves use [def-pur-hom-complex]. In each total degree $h\otimes x$ has finite support in the tensor direct sum, so this formula defines a map into every product component of the double Hom, even for unbounded complexes. The formula is a chain map because it is a transpose of chain evaluation; the cited chain tensor--Hom isomorphism supplies precisely compatibility with the differentials. Thus it is the chain representative of the already canonical map, with no extra descent or functorial-choice assertion.

source.place: Tags 0A67 and 0A60, the representative construction and remark-sign-explanation

proof.text: For $F$, present any distinguished triangle by a cone triangle of K-flat complexes $P_1\to P_2\to C\to P_1[1]$ using [lem-pc-kflat-cone-triangle-presentation]. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] with the arbitrary coefficient complex $A^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(J,I)$. Explicitly the cone isomorphism sends $h\otimes(y,x)$ to $(h\otimes y,(-1)^a h\otimes x)$ for $|h|=a$, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Its first component preserves the inclusion; its second component identifies the projection with the tensor shift map $A^\bullet\otimes P_1[1]\to(A^\bullet\otimes P_1)[1]$, whose multiplier is $(-1)^a$. It therefore also respects the negative projection used for the connecting map in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This proves exactness of $F$ with that shift comparison. For $G$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] twice in its first variable, first with target $L$, then with target $M$. The two reversals give a covariant exact functor. Use the signed composite comparison: the two contravariant shift identifications and the sign from the reversal of triangles. This includes the customary extra minus for the shift by one.

Check the signed comparisons on the representatives of step 3. With the Hom differential of [def-pur-hom-complex], the first-variable comparison $s_{P,m}:\operatorname{Hom}(P[m],J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,J)[-m]$ multiplies a homogeneous map of degree $q$ by $(-1)^{mq}$ and reindexes its source. Substitution in $d(f)=d_Jf-(-1)^qfd_P$ verifies this chain identity; replacing $J$ by $I$ gives the outer comparison. Their signed composite for $G(P[m])\to G(P)[m]$ is
$$\chi_{P,m}=(-1)^m s_{H(P,J),-m}\circ H(s_{P,m},I)^{-1}.$$
On $g\in G(P[m])^n$ tested at $f\in H(P,J)^c$, this reads $(\chi_{P,m}g)(f)=(-1)^{m(n+c)}g(f)$, where $f$ on the right is read in $H(P[m],J)^{c+m}$. Indeed the two reindexings contribute $m(c+m)+mn$, and the reversal contributes $m$; $m^2+m$ is even. Tensor shift has multiplier $(-1)^{ma}$ on $h\otimes x$. If $x\in P^b$, its degree in $P[m]$ is $b-m$ and $n=a+b-m$. Consequently
$$(b-m)(c+m)+m(n+c)\equiv bc+ma\pmod2.$$
The left side is the sign of $\chi_{P,m}E_{P[m]}$, and the right side that of $E_P[m]$ after tensor shift. Hence the shift square commutes for every integer $m$. These are the signed exactness comparisons of step 4, not unsigned reindexings. The identity passes to $D(R)$ through the representative comparisons of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

source.place: Tag 0A60, lemma-evaluate-and-more, remark-sign-explanation and section-sign-rules; signed double contravariant shift calculation expanding sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JC

proof.text:
Let $K_1\xrightarrow{u}K_2\xrightarrow{v}K_3\xrightarrow{w}K_1[1]$ be distinguished. Step 4 makes its $F$ and $G$ images distinguished. Step 2 gives $G(u)e_1=e_2F(u)$ and $G(v)e_2=e_3F(v)$, and also $G(w)e_3=e_{K_1[1]}F(w)$. Write $\varphi:F(K_1[1])\to F(K_1)[1]$ and $\psi:G(K_1[1])\to G(K_1)[1]$ for step 4's comparisons. Step 5 gives $\psi e_{K_1[1]}=e_1[1]\varphi$, so
$$\psi G(w)e_3=e_1[1]\varphi F(w).$$
This is exactly the square on the connecting arrows in the definition of a morphism of triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus all three components define the asserted morphism of distinguished triangles. No argument has required $e_i$ to be invertible.
